- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.67), especially in early forecast periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.50), particularly in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- Avoid sharp upward forecasts when sentiment is weak or recently negative; model tends to overreact.
- Correct for mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is rising (last 3 days > 0.75), model tends to overforecast; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is > 10% above forecast, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if yes, adjust downward slightly to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment is consistently low (last 5 days < 0.33), model tends to underestimate — add 2–5% to forecast to compensate.
